description: The image presents two pie charts comparing the distribution of error types and correct responses across two distinct categories, likely representing performance on different task types or student groups, as referenced in the paper “Laying the Foundation First: Investigating the Generalization from Atomic Skills to Complex Reasoning Tasks.” The legend identifies four categories: “Atomic Skill Fail” (dark teal), “Correct” (medium teal), “Reason Error” (light teal), and “Question Misunderstood” (white). In the left pie chart, “Atomic Skill Fail” dominates at 68.0%, followed by “Correct” and “Reason Error” each at 12.0%, and “Question Misunderstood” at 8.0%. In the right pie chart, “Correct” is the largest segment at 55.0%, followed by “Reason Error” at 21.0%, “Question Misunderstood” at 14.0%, and “Atomic Skill Fail” at 10.0%. The visual contrast between the two charts suggests a shift in performance profile—where the left chart reflects heavy reliance on or failure of atomic skills, and the right chart shows greater success with more balanced error distribution, possibly indicating improved generalization to complex reasoning tasks. Each slice is labeled with its percentage, and the charts are presented side-by-side for direct comparison, with no exploded segments or additional annotations.
